782-about-the-department-of-mechanical-e: Mechanical systems for aerospace, energy, robotics, manufacturing, medical devices and transport, grounded in math, science, solids, fluids, thermodynamics, dynamics and control, with hands-on design ending in a team capstone.

Options: Honours for research, a Minor in Aerospace, technical electives, and minors in other faculties, often with one extra semester. Student design teams include Formula Electric, Baja, Robotics, Rocket and AERO, with MAME and EUS.
782-location: Macdonald Engineering Building, Room 270, 817 Sherbrooke St. W.
782-program-description: Design and manufacturing, materials and solids, thermodynamics and fluids, dynamics and control, mechatronics, and modelling, applied through experiments and design. Focus areas: industrial, numerical methods, robotics, bioengineering, aeronautics, energy and systems.
783-technical-complementary-courses-15-c: 6 at 500+ in MECH. 9 at 300+ in Engineering or Science, or approved Group A and B courses.
784-faculty-of-arts: 200–300 in listed departments, not seminars, field, survey or topics courses or reserved ones, with some exclusions.
784-faculty-of-engineering: Management and ENVR have limits. INTG 215 isn't open after INTG 201 and 202.
784-program-description: Not currently offered. The same disciplines with supervised research; limited, competitive, with no first-year entry.
785-technical-complementary-courses-18-c: 8 from the list, 4 of Honours thematic courses, 6 at 400+ in Engineering or Science, with your coordinator or supervisor.
787-program-description: Not currently offered. Five design courses, 15–16 credits, including an interdisciplinary project. Declare with a Course Authorization Form.
788-about-the-department-of-mining-and-m: B.Eng. in Materials or Mining, with seminars, colloquia, projects and field trips to industrial sites.
788-scholarships: Renewable Entrance Scholarships, and others from the Department, Canadian Mineral Industry Education Foundation, CIM Foundation and Québec Mining Association.
788-co-op-in-materials-engineering: CEAB-accredited with industrial work terms: processing, fabrication, applications and performance, with labs. Leads to resource and manufacturing jobs.
Co-op fee $273.76 over ten terms, $2,737.60 in all. Register for each training course on time, with the Liaison Officer's approval first.
788-student-advising: Plan your schedule with a departmental adviser; book through the Coordinator.
788-co-op-in-mining-engineering: Canada's oldest mining program, since 1871: mining science, mineral economics, planning, rock mechanics, renewable energy and mine design. Accredited, with three paid work terms and a dedicated Liaison Officer.

English stream from high school; Bilingual from CEGEP, with six courses at Polytechnique Montréal. Scholarships and support for mining competitions. Register for MIME 290, 291 and 392; a fourth term can be complementary and a fifth extra.
788-student-advising-2: You're assigned an adviser for your whole degree, and meet at least yearly.
789-location: Wong Building, Room 2140, 3610 University St. Mining: Adams Building, Room 125, 3450 University St.
789-program-description: Admission is only to the Co-op; you can transfer to this non-co-op Major with approval. The materials pipeline from ore to microstructures to uses in aerospace, electronics and biology. Specialize or broaden with complementaries.
790-technical-complementaries-18-credits: 12–18 from the list. CHEE 515 or MIME 515, in alternate years. 6 may be outside the Department with approval.
791-program-description: The materials pipeline from ore to uses, plus three work terms. Plan with an adviser.
792-technical-complementaries-12-credits: 9–12 from the list. CHEE 515 or MIME 515. 0–3 outside the Department with approval.
794-program-description: Needs departmental approval. Sustainable extraction of mineral resources, in English or Bilingual streams, with field trips.
794-b-eng-major-in-mining-engineering: 144–145 credits. Admission is only to the Co-op; transfer in any time with the adviser's approval and a Course Authorization form.
795-list-b: 0–6 from the list or other technical courses with approval. Not all run yearly. Some are at Polytechnique.
797-program-description: Sustainable extraction, in two streams, with field trips and three work terms. Register and pay by add/drop, with the Liaison Officer's approval.
799-faculty-of-arts: 200–300 in listed departments or listed Management, Science and Engineering courses, with the usual exclusions. Language courses no longer count for Group B, for those entering from Fall 2017.
